In this connection, we are pleased to inform you that the single filing system has been extended for Integrated Filing (Financials) under Regulation 33 of SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015 with effect from January 03, 2026. The single filing system through API-based integration shall be available for the following disclosures: Particulars Regulation as per SEBI (LODR)Reg ulations 2015/ SEBI (Depositories & Participants) Regulations 2018 Effective date Type of Listed Companies Only Equity Equity+ Debt Exclusively Debt REITs and INVIT Integrated Filing (Financials) 23(9), Reg 30 r/w Section V-B of the Master circular, 32(1) & 33(3) January 03, 2026 √ √ shall be communicat ed later shall be communicated later Annual Secretarial Compliance Report 24A (2) September 15, 2025 √ √ shall be communicat ed later shall be communicated later Integrated Filing (Governance) 13 (3), 27 (2) & 30 March 01, 2025 √ √ shall be communicat ed later shall be communicated later Meetings of shareholders 44 (3) December 28, 2024 √ √ - - Particulars Regulation as per SEBI (LODR)Reg ulations 2015/ SEBI (Depositories & Participants) Regulations 2018 Effective date Type of Listed Companies Only Equity Equity+ Debt Exclusively Debt REITs and INVIT and Voting Results Reconciliation of Share Capital Audit Report 76 November 15, 2024 √ √ - - Corporate Governance Report 27 (2) October 26, 2024 Merged with Integrated Filing (Governance) pursuant to the SEBI Circular dated December 31, 2024. shall be communicat ed later shall be communicated later Investor Grievance Report 13
rows.summary:
The National Stock Exchange of India has updated its “single filing system” for API-based integration between stock exchanges by extending the system to **Integrated Filing (Financials)** under **Regulation 33 of the SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015**, effective **January 03, 2026**. This means listed entities covered by the framework will be able to submit the specified disclosures once through the integrated API-based process rather than making duplicate filings on both exchanges, with the explicit intent of reducing multiple submissions of the same information.

The circular confirms the following disclosure categories and their rollout status: **Integrated Filing (Financials)** applies from **January 03, 2026** for **equity-only** and **equity+debt** listed companies, while the applicability for **exclusively debt** listed companies and for **REITs/InvITs** will be **communicated later**. It also notes that **Annual Secretarial Compliance Report** under **Regulation 24A(2)** has an effective date of **September 15, 2025** for equity-only and equity+debt entities, with the debt-only and REIT/InvIT applicability still pending. **Integrated Filing (Governance)** under **Regulations 13(3), 27(2), and 30** became effective **March 01, 2025** for equity-only and equity+debt entities; **Meetings of shareholders and Voting Results** under **Regulation 44(3)** became effective **December 28, 2024** for equity-only and equity+debt entities; and **Reconciliation of Share Capital Audit Report** under **Regulation 76** became effective **November 15, 2024** for equity-only and equity+debt entities. The **Corporate Governance Report** under **Regulation 27(2)** had an effective date of **October 26, 2024**, but the circular states it has been **merged with Integrated Filing (Governance) pursuant to the SEBI circular dated December 31, 2024**. The **Investor Grievance Report** under **Regulation 13(3)** became effective **October 1, 2024**, with applicability shown for equity-only entities and debt/reit/invIT categories still to be communicated later.

For compliance purposes, the key procedural requirement is that listed entities should **not file the same disclosure multiple times on both exchanges** once the single filing system applies. If one exchange seeks clarification after a submission, the entity must respond **to the exchange that raised the clarification**, rather than routing responses elsewhere. The NSE directs listed entities to comply accordingly and provides support contacts through **NEAPS > Help > Contact Us > Listing Compliance**, or by email to **takeover@nse.co.in**; queries specifically relating to **Integrated Filing (Financials)** should be sent to **listingfr@nse.co.in**.

rows.title: SEBI Circular on “Minimum information to be provided to the Audit Committee and Shareholders for approval of Related Party Transactions.”

No.: NSE/CML/2025/38 Date: October 09, 2025 To, All Real Estate Investment Trusts (REITs) All Infrastructure Investment Trusts (InvITs) Subject: Filing of Financial Results by REITs & InvITs in XBRL Mode This is in reference to the SEBI Master circular SEBI/HO/DDHS-PoD-2/P/CIR/2025/99 dated July 11, 2025, for REITs & SEBI Master circular SEBI/HO/DDHS-PoD-2/P/CIR/2025/102 dated July 11, 2025, for InvITs, regarding Chapter 4 - Continuous Disclosures and Compliances by REITs & InvITs wherein the format for submission of financial results by REITs & InvITs has been revised as per the aforesaid Master circulars. In this regard, we wish to inform you that the excel utility for submission of Financial Results-REITs & InvITs as per the revised format has been made available on NEAPS portal on the below path: Compliance > Common XBRL Upload > Invit/Reit- Financial Results The REITs & InvITs are required to submit the financial results in XBRL mode within 24 hours of submission of the financial results in PDF mode using the excel utility “Financial Results_Invits_Reits” In case of any queries concerning the captioned subject, you may contact the respective team members on the contact details available in the NEAPS platform at path NEAPS > Help > Contact Us > Listing Compliance or send an email to listingfr@nse.co.in Yours faithfully, For National Stock Exchange of India Limited Mandar Walavalkar Vice President-Listing
rows.summary:
The National Stock Exchange of India (NSE) has issued a listing circular dated October 9, 2025 (Ref. No. NSE/CML/2025/38) addressed to all REITs and InvITs, informing them of a revised filing requirement for financial results under the SEBI Master Circulars dated July 11, 2025: SEBI/HO/DDHS-PoD-2/P/CIR/2025/99 for REITs and SEBI/HO/DDHS-PoD-2/P/CIR/2025/102 for InvITs. The circular states that, pursuant to Chapter 4 on Continuous Disclosures and Compliances, the format for submission of financial results by REITs and InvITs has been revised, and NSE has now made available an updated Excel utility on the NEAPS portal for XBRL submission.

Operationally, REITs and InvITs must continue submitting financial results in PDF mode and then file the same financial results in XBRL mode within 24 hours of the PDF submission. The specified utility to be used is “Financial Results_Invits_Reits,” and it can be accessed through NEAPS at: Compliance > Common XBRL Upload > Invit/Reit- Financial Results. This means the compliance obligation is not just to file financial results, but to ensure the XBRL filing is completed on a tight 24-hour follow-on timeline using the prescribed utility and revised format.

For questions, entities are directed to the relevant NEAPS support contacts under NEAPS > Help > Contact Us > Listing Compliance, or by email to listingfr@nse.co.in. The circular applies specifically to REITs and InvITs subject to NSE/SEBI continuous disclosure requirements, and it reflects an implementation/update to the filing format rather than a change to the underlying financial results content itself.

rows.summary:
The National Stock Exchange of India (NSE) has expanded its “single filing system” via API-based integration between stock exchanges to cover the **Annual Secretarial Compliance Report** required under **Regulation 24A(2) of the SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015**, with an **effective date of September 15, 2025**. This means that, for entities covered by the feature, the report can now be filed once through the integrated system rather than separately on both exchanges, as part of NSE’s broader move toward consolidated filing across exchanges.

The circular reiterates that the single-filing mechanism is intended to prevent **multiple filings of the same disclosure on both exchanges**. If one exchange seeks clarification after submission, the listed entity must respond to **that specific exchange** that raised the query, rather than duplicating the response elsewhere. Compliance teams should therefore ensure their internal filing procedures are aligned so that the same document is not resubmitted redundantly on both venues unless specifically required.

As set out in the circular’s table, the single filing system already applies or is being rolled out for several other disclosures: **Investor Grievance Report under Regulation 13(3)** (effective **October 1, 2024**, and later **merged with Integrated Filing (Governance)** pursuant to the SEBI circular dated **December 31, 2024**); **Corporate Governance Report under Regulation 27(2)** (effective **October 26, 2024**, with availability for some entity categories noted as “shall be communicated later”); **Reconciliation of Share Capital Audit Report under Regulation 76** (effective **November 15, 2024**); **Meetings of shareholders and Voting Results under Regulation 44(3)** (effective **December 28, 2024**); and **Integrated Filing (Governance) under Regulations 13(3), 27(2), and 30** (effective **March 1, 2025**). For the **Annual Secretarial Compliance Report**, the table indicates applicability to **equity-listed companies** and **equity + debt listed companies** from **September 15, 2025**, while applicability to **exclusively debt-listed entities** and **REITs/InvITs** is listed as **“shall be communicated later.”**

In practical terms, any listed entity that falls within the categories already enabled for the system should review its filing workflow, confirm use of the API-integrated process, and ensure the report is filed only once through the appropriate exchange interface. The circular does not create a new substantive reporting standard for the Annual Secretarial Compliance Report itself; rather, it changes the **filing mechanism** and the expectations around duplicate submissions and clarification handling. For assistance, NSE directs listed entities to the **NEAPS platform** under **NEAPS > Help > Contact Us > Listing Compliance** or to email **takeover@nse.co.in**.

rows.desc: National Stock Exchange of India Circular Department: Listing Circular Ref. No.: NSE/CML/2025/36 Date: September 04, 2025 To, All Listed Entities Subject: Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) on Applicability of the Industry Standards on “Minimum information to be provided for Review of the Audit Committee and Shareholders for Approval of Related Party Transaction (RPT)” Dear Sir / Madam, This has reference to SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/CFD/CFD-PoD-2/P/CIR/2025/93 dated June 26, 2025, with respect to the Industry Standards on Minimum information to be provided for review of the audit committee and shareholders for approval of a related party transaction. In this connection, Frequently Asked Questions (FAQS) on the Industry Standards on “Minimum information to be provided for Review of the Audit Committee and Shareholders for Approval of Related Party Transaction (RPT)”, are enclosed for your reference and necessary action. The copy of the circular is also available on the NSE website (www.nseindia.com) Yours Faithfully For National Stock Exchange of India Ltd. Saba Curtay Chief Manager- Listing Compliance Encl: 1. Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) on the Industry Standards on “Minimum information to be provided for Review of the Audit Committee and Shareholders for Approval of Related Party Transaction (RPT)”. Frequently Asked Questions on the RPT Industry Standards 1. Does the RPT Industry Standards replace all previous RPT disclosure formats as prescribed under Section III-B of Master Circular for compliance with the provisions of the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 by listed entities dated 11 th November, 2024 (“Master Circular”)? Yes. It substitutes the disclosure requirement as specified in the Section III-B of the Master Circular from the specified date. If a particular part of the RPT Industry Standards is inconsistent with subsequent amendments in the LODR Regulations and/or SEBI Circular
rows.summary:
This NSE circular dated September 4, 2025 forwards FAQs on the SEBI-mandated Industry Standards for the minimum information to be placed before the Audit Committee and shareholders for approval of related party transactions (“RPTs”). The circular makes clear that these Industry Standards **replace** the earlier RPT disclosure formats in **Section III-B of the NSE Master Circular dated November 11, 2024**, from the **specified effective date**, but if any part of the Industry Standards conflicts with later amendments to the LODR Regulations or subsequent SEBI circulars, the **LODR Regulations/SEBI circulars prevail**.

For compliance purposes, the Industry Standards are described as setting only the **minimum** information to be disclosed; listed entities may provide **additional information** to the Audit Committee and/or shareholders if management believes it is in the interest of public shareholders, and the Audit Committee may itself seek further information where it considers that necessary and reasonable to assess the proposed RPT. The FAQs confirm the **effective date is 1 September 2025** under SEBI Circular No. **SEBI/HO/CFD/CFD-PoD-2/P/CIR/2025/93 dated June 26, 2025**.

The applicability is broad: the Standards apply not only to direct RPTs of the listed entity, but also to RPTs involving **foreign subsidiaries of Indian listed companies** and to transactions undertaken by **subsidiaries where the listed entity itself is not a party**, so long as those transactions require Audit Committee and/or shareholder approval of the listed holding company under the LODR Regulations. The FAQs also state that where the listed entity has RPTs with **fellow subsidiaries**, the holding company may provide a **duly certified summary of financial information** for the relevant subsidiaries to support Audit Committee/shareholder review, but this is subject to a caveat that the information is based on data collected for preparation of the listed entity’s **consolidated financial statements**.

The FAQs further clarify that the Standards are not limited to the specific transaction types covered in Part B and Part C; **Part A of Para 4 applies to all related party transactions unless exempt under Para 1(3)**. The document begins to address a threshold aggregation example involving three RPTs of **₹30 lakh each** and a fourth proposed transaction of **₹11 lakh**, indicating that numerical aggregation/threshold treatment is a compliance issue under the Standards, but the provided text cuts off before the answer is completed.

rows.summary:
This NSE circular announces a new **system-driven disclosure mechanism** for both **credit rating disclosures under Regulation 30(6) read with sub-para 3 of Para A of Part A of Schedule III of SEBI LODR** and for **ESG rating disclosures**, effective **August 02, 2025**. It is issued in light of SEBI’s December 31, 2024 circular on ease-of-doing-business measures for listed entities and SEBI’s April 29, 2025 circular on clarificatory/procedural changes for ESG Rating Providers (ERPs). Under the new arrangement, **stock exchanges will consume rating data directly from CRAs and ERPs and automatically disseminate it on the exchange website**, rather than relying on separate manual/public disclosure processes, and NSE has created dedicated web paths for these disclosures: one for credit rating disclosures and one for ESG rating disclosures.

The circular applies to **all listed entities**, **all SEBI-registered Credit Rating Agencies (CRAs)**, and **all SEBI-registered ESG Rating Providers (ERPs)**. For **credit ratings**, the system covers **“new rating(s) or revision in ratings”** required to be disclosed under the cited LODR provision. For **ESG ratings**, the exchange will prominently display ESG ratings on the listed company’s page for **issuer/entity-level ESG ratings** and on the listed security’s page for **debt-security ESG ratings**, consistent with the April 29, 2025 SEBI circular.

CRAs and ERPs are instructed to use the **NEAPS** portal on a **daily basis** to upload the required rating data. The prescribed workflow is: log in to **https://neaps.nseindia.com/NEWLISTINGCORP/**, then CRAs must select **“SDD- Creating Rating- Reg. 30”** while ERPs must select **“SSD- Credit Rating- ESG- Equity”** for equity-listed entities or **“ESG Rating- Debt”** for debt-listed entities. They must download the Excel template, fill in the required details, and upload it back through the system; the circular notes that the **name and symbol of the listed entity are auto-captured from the ISIN entered**, so the ISIN is the key input for identifying the issuer/security. NSE also points users to its public ISIN reference pages for equity-listed entities and debt private placements so the correct identifiers can be used.

Once uploaded, the information will be **auto-disseminated on the NSE website** at the specified rating disclosure pages. NSE has stated that **login credentials are being provided to all SEBI-registered CRAs and ERPs**, and any operational questions should be raised through **NEAPS > Help > Contact Us > Listing Compliance** or by emailing **takeover@nse.co.in**.

rows.summary:
This NSE circular, issued on July 7, 2025 (Ref. No. NSE/CML/2025/30), expands the XBRL filing functionality on the NEAPS platform to cover Regulation 30 disclosures relating to the **awarding, bagging/receiving, amendment, or termination of orders/contracts**, whether in the ordinary course of business or otherwise. The Exchange states that this XBRL facility is **effective immediately from July 7, 2025**.

For compliance purposes, listed entities must first submit the disclosure in **PDF format** on the Exchange, and at this initial stage the PDF filing will be treated by NSE as sufficient compliance with Regulation 30 of the SEBI LODR Regulations, 2015. However, this is not the end of the obligation: the entity must then file the corresponding **XBRL submission within 24 hours of the PDF filing**. The XBRL utility is available in NEAPS under **COMPLIANCE >> Common XBRL Upload >> Equity Announcement-XBRL >> Awarding or Bagging of Orders/Contracts**.

NSE also says that the XBRL filing will be made available in **iXBRL format** on the Exchange website and in NEAPS under **Report >> Announcement XBRL Report**. The circular specifically warns that companies have been filing these disclosures under **Updates** or **Press Release**, and directs that such disclosures must instead be filed under the **Announcement** section using the subject **“Awarding/Bagging/Receiving of order(s)/contract(s) (whether in normal course of business or not in normal course of business)”**, with the necessary parameters required by the SEBI circular. For questions, listed entities are told to use the NEAPS **Help > Contact Us > Listing Compliance** path or email **takeover@nse.co.in**.

In this connection, this is to inform you that the XBRL utility for Integrated Filing - Financial has been made available on NEAPS portal on the below path: Compliance > Common XBRL Upload > Integrated Filing > Integrated Filing- Financial Listed entities are required to submit financial results in XBRL mode using “Integrated Filing-Financial” utility only. Note: 1. Outcome of the Board Meeting in PDF mode for Financial Results to be submitted within the prescribed timelines of 30 mins or 3 hours as may be applicable, on the below path only: Compliance > Announcements/Corporate actions > Create announcement/ corporate actions > Intimation type: Announcement > Regulation 30 – Para A > Subject – Outcome of board meeting > Type – Financial results 2. Further, the listed entities shall submit Integrated Filing - Financial in XBRL on same date of submission of the financial results (in PDF form), on the below path only: Compliance > Common XBRL Upload > Integrated Filing > Integrated Filing - Financial Please note that the following shall be discontinued w.e.f. April 01, 2025: 1. Financial results submitted in PDF form under NEAPS - Quick Results tab 2. PDF filing of ‘Integrated Filing - Financial’ in the Corporate Announcement under following path: NEAPS > Compliance > Announcements > Announcements/C
rows.summary:
The National Stock Exchange of India’s circular dated April 2, 2025 (Ref. No. NSE/CML/2025/20) updates listed entities on implementation of the Expert Committee recommendations on “ease of doing business” and specifically the disclosure process for **Integrated Filing – Financial**. The circular refers to SEBI Circular **SEBI/HO/CFD/CFD-PoD-2/CIR/P/2024/185 dated December 31, 2024** and NSE circular **NSE/CML/2025/02 dated January 2, 2025**, and confirms that the **XBRL utility for Integrated Filing – Financial is now available on the NEAPS portal** at **Compliance > Common XBRL Upload > Integrated Filing > Integrated Filing- Financial**.

For **all listed entities**, financial results must now be filed in **XBRL mode only through the “Integrated Filing-Financial” utility**. In addition, the **Board Meeting outcome for financial results** must still be filed in **PDF format** within the applicable statutory timeline of **30 minutes or 3 hours** (depending on the applicable disclosure timeline), and that PDF filing must be made only through **Compliance > Announcements/Corporate actions > Create announcement/corporate actions > Intimation type: Announcement > Regulation 30 – Para A > Subject – Outcome of board meeting > Type – Financial results**. The circular also requires that the **Integrated Filing – Financial XBRL submission be made on the same date as the PDF submission of the financial results** and only through **Compliance > Common XBRL Upload > Integrated Filing > Integrated Filing - Financial**.

A key compliance change is that, **effective April 1, 2025**, several older filing routes are discontinued. These include: (1) filing **financial results in PDF** under the **NEAPS Quick Results tab**; (2) filing **“Integrated Filing - Financial” in PDF** under the Corporate Announcement path (**NEAPS > Compliance > Announcements > Announcements/Corporate Actions > Create Announcement**); (3) the **existing XBRL utilities** for **Financial Results**, **Related Party Transactions Disclosure**, **Statement of Deviations**, and **Impact of Audit Qualifications**; and (4) submission of **Statement of Deviation(s) / variation(s)** in **PDF format**. Compliance teams should therefore ensure they are using the new Integrated Filing-Financial XBRL workflow and that legacy upload methods are no longer used after the April 1, 2025 cutoff.

For operational support, NSE directs listed entities to use the contact details available on NEAPS under **NEAPS > Help > Contact Us > Listing Compliance** or email **listingfr@nse.co.in**.

rows.desc: National Stock Exchange of India Circular Department: Listing Circular Ref. No.: NSE/CML/2025/17 Date: April 01, 2025 To, The Company Secretaries, All Listed Entities Subject: SEBI Circular on Measures to facilitate ease of doing business with respect to framework for assurance or assessment, ESG disclosures for value chain, and introduction of voluntary disclosure on green credits. This has reference to the SEBI circular No. SEBI/HO/CFD/CFD-PoD-1/P/CIR/2025/42 dated March 28, 2025 (“SEBI Circular”) regarding implementation of recommendations of the Expert Committee for facilitating ease of doing business for listed entities respect to framework for assurance or assessment, ESG disclosures for value chain, and introduction of voluntary disclosure on green credits. A copy of SEBI Circular dated March 28, 2025, is enclosed for reference and necessary action at your end. The copy of the circular is also available on the NSE website (www.nseindia.com). This is for your information please. Yours faithfully, For National Stock Exchange of India Limited Apeksha Raichura Manager – Listing Compliance Encl: 1. SEBI Circular Page 1 of 4 CIRCULAR SEBI/HO/CFD/CFD-PoD-1/P/CIR/2025/42 March 28, 2025 To, All listed entities All the recognized Stock Exchanges Dear Sir/Madam, Sub: Measures to facilitate ease of doing business with respect to framework for assurance or assessment, ESG disclosures for value chain, and introduction of voluntary disclosure on green credits. 1. Based on the recommendations of the Expert Committee for Facilitating Ease of Doing Business and pursuant to public consultation, the Board, on December 18, 2024, decided to revise various provisions regarding ESG disclosures for value chain, provide an option to undertake ‘assessment’ or ‘assurance’ for BRSR Core and ESG disclosures for value chain, and introduce disclosure on green credits. 2. Accordingly, the provisions of SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 (“LODR Regulation
rows.summary:
This SEBI circular, dated March 28, 2025 and circulated by NSE on April 1, 2025, revises the ESG/BRSR framework to make assurance/assessment processes easier and adds new disclosure requirements. SEBI says these changes follow Expert Committee recommendations and public consultation, and they have already been implemented through amendments to the LODR Regulations via Gazette ID CG-MH-E-28032025-262027 dated March 28, 2025. The circular also partially modifies the November 11, 2024 Master Circular on LODR compliance, so listed entities need to update their ESG reporting and verification processes accordingly.

For BRSR, SEBI has added a new eighth leadership indicator under Principle 6 in Annexure 16 requiring disclosure of how many Green Credits have been generated or procured, separately for (a) the listed entity and (b) the top ten value chain partners, ranked by value of purchases and sales respectively. This new green credits disclosure applies to BRSR filings for FY 2024–25 onward.

For BRSR Core and ESG disclosures for the value chain, SEBI has changed the framework so listed entities may use either “assessment” or “assurance,” and the process is intended to be profession-agnostic. The circular clarifies that “assessment” means a third-party assessment carried out under standards developed by the Industry Standards Forum (ISF) in consultation with SEBI. It also states that the methodology in BRSR Core is only a base methodology, and any changes or industry-specific adjustments/estimations must be disclosed, so companies cannot silently modify the approach. The revised BRSR Core is described as a sub-set of BRSR containing KPIs/metrics across 9 ESG attributes, with some new metrics tailored to the Indian/emerging-market context such as job creation in small towns, openness of business, and gross wages paid to women, and it also includes intensity ratios based on revenue adjusted for Purchasing Power Parity (PPP).

The circular further states that listed entities must mandatorily undertake assessment or assurance of BRSR Core according to a glide path, with the detailed applicability table to be used for phased compliance. Because the document excerpt provided cuts off before the full glide path table, compliance teams should review the full SEBI circular and updated master circular annexures to confirm exactly when their company falls into the mandatory assessment/assurance regime and which reporting year applies. In practice, the main action items are to update ESG reporting templates for the new green credits disclosure, align internal controls and vendor/value-chain data collection for BRSR Core, and ensure the chosen verification route and methodology disclosures conform to the revised SEBI/ISF standards.

The new framework for Rights Issue process has been introduced vide notification of SEBI (Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements) (Amendment) Regulations, 2025, with Gazette ID CG-DL-E-08032025-261516 published in the Official Gazette on March 08, 2025. The same is available at this link. 2. As part of the new framework, in terms of amended Regulation 85 of SEBI (Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2018 (SEBI ICDR Regulations), it is being specified that Rights Issues shall be completed within 23 working days from the date of Board of Directors of the Issuer approving the Rights Issue. 3. Accordingly, the revised timelines for completion of the various activ
rows.summary:
SEBI’s March 11, 2025 circular introduces a new framework for rights issues under the amended SEBI ICDR Regulations, 2018, and the NSE circular dated March 12, 2025 simply forwards it to listed entities and registered merchant bankers for necessary action. The key change is that a rights issue must now be completed within **23 working days from the date the issuer’s Board of Directors approves the rights issue**; SEBI also says that where the rights issue is for **convertible debt instruments** and shareholder approval is required, the timetable must be adjusted to account for that approval step. Correspondingly, the rights issue subscription window must remain open for **at least 7 days and no more than 30 days**.

SEBI has also revised the operational workflow: **stock exchanges and depositories, together with the registrar to the issue, must validate subscription bids and finalize the basis of allotment**, and the exchanges and depositories must develop an **automated investor application validation system within 6 months from the circular’s applicable date**. This is a material process requirement for the market infrastructure institutions involved in rights issues, and issuers and intermediaries should expect the new validation and allotment process to be integrated into the shortened timeline.

The circular also makes several consequential updates to the SEBI master circular for ICDR matters. Issuers must disclose in the **letter of offer** the process for **credit of rights entitlements (REs) to demat accounts and their renunciation**. For application mechanics, SEBI states that applicants may use the **application form available on the registrar’s website or printed forms sourced from the issuer or registrar**. A further procedural change requires that **correction of bid data collated by the self-certified syndicate bank (SCSB) after issue closure must be completed on the issue closure date itself**.

Finally, for filing and fee payment, rights issue issuers must **file the letter of offer with SEBI by email at cfddil@sebi.gov.in** and pay the filing fee **online through the SEBI website payment link under the “Filing Fees” category**. The circular also references partial modifications to the master circular’s public-issue review provisions, indicating that the SEBI filing framework is being aligned with the new faster rights issue process. Overall, the document primarily affects **listed entities planning rights issues, merchant bankers, stock exchanges, depositories, registrars, bankers to an issue, SCSBs, and NPCI**, with the substantive compliance impact centered on tighter timelines, revised bid-validation responsibilities, and updated filing/disclosure procedures.

rows.title: Clarification on fixing the record date under Regulation 42 of SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015
rows.desc: Department: LISTING Circular Ref. No: NSE/CML/2025/04 Date: February 07, 2025 To All Listed Entities, Subject: Clarification on fixing the record date under Regulation 42 of SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 This is with reference to the recent amendment made by the Securities and Exchange Board of India to regulation 42 of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements), Regulations, 2015 vide notification dated December 12, 2024. It is clarified that listed entities shall ensure a minimum gap of at least three working days between the date of board/shareholders’ approval, as applicable to the specific corporate action mentioned in Regulation 42 (1), and the Record Date fixed for such purpose. The minimum gap shall be exclusive of the date of board/shareholder's approval and the actual record date. Further, as per latest amendment, sub-regulation 5 of Regulation 42 of SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements), Regulations, 2015 has been omitted. Hence the listed entities are not required to announce dates of closure of their transfer books for any purpose. All Listed entities are requested to take note of the same and comply accordingly. For and on behalf of National Stock Exchange of India Limited Senior Manager Harshad Dharod
rows.summary:
This circular clarifies how listed entities must fix the **record date** under **Regulation 42 of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015** following SEBI’s amendment notified on **December 12, 2024**. From this clarification, a listed entity must ensure a **minimum gap of at least three working days** between the **date of board approval or shareholders’ approval** (depending on what is applicable for the relevant corporate action under Regulation 42(1)) and the **record date** set for that corporate action. The three-working-day gap must be calculated **excluding both the approval date and the actual record date**, so the intervening working days are what matter.

The circular also notes a separate compliance change: **Regulation 42(5) has been omitted**. As a result, listed entities are **no longer required to announce closure dates of transfer books for any purpose**. This applies to **all listed entities** and to any corporate action covered by **Regulation 42(1)**. The circular is dated **February 07, 2025**, and the exchange instructs listed entities to take note and **comply accordingly**.

rows.desc: Non-Confidential Circular Department: Listing Circular Ref No: NSE/CML/2025/02 Date: January 02, 2025 To, The Company Secretaries, All Listed Entities Subject: Implementation of recommendations of the Expert Committee for facilitating ease of doing business for listed entities This has reference to the amendments to the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 (“SEBI LODR”) which have been published in the Gazette of India on December 13, 2024 and to give effect to certain recommendations of the Expert Committee and carry out consequential changes to the provisions of SEBI Master Circular dated November 11, 2024, on compliance with the SEBI LODR by listed entities, SEBI has issued a circular SEBI/HO/CFD/CFD-PoD-2/CIR/P/2024/185 dated December 31, 2024 (‘SEBI Circular’). In this regard a copy of SEBI Circular dated December 31, 2024, is enclosed for your reference and for necessary action at your end. The copy of the circular will also be made available on the NSE website at https://www.nseindia.com/companies- listing/circular-for-listed-companies-equity-market Based on the above, the Integrated Filing shall be applicable for the filings to be done for the quarter ending December 31, 2024, and thereafter. The timelines for Integrated Filing shall be as follows: a. Integrated Filing (Governance): within 30 days from the end of the quarter; b. Integrated Filing (Financial): within 45 days from the end of the quarter, other than the last quarter, and 60 days from the end of the last quarter and the financial year In this regard, the first quarterly Integrated Filing i.e. Integrated Filing (Governance) and Integrated Filing (Financial) which is applicable for the quarter ending December 31, 2024, may be filed within a period of 45 days from the end of the quarter. However, for subsequent quarterly filings, the companies shall follow the timelines as mentioned under point a & b above. Note: Basis the above
rows.summary:
This circular from the National Stock Exchange implements SEBI’s December 31, 2024 circular and the related amendments to the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015, which were published in the Gazette of India on December 13, 2024. Its main effect is to introduce “Integrated Filing” for listed entities, with separate PDF submissions for governance and financial disclosures using the SEBI-prescribed format, while the existing XBRL/PDF filings for the underlying compliances must continue until further notice. The new regime applies to filings for the quarter ending December 31, 2024 and thereafter.

For timing, the first quarterly Integrated Filing for the December 31, 2024 quarter may be submitted within 45 days from quarter-end, but after that the deadlines split: Integrated Filing (Governance) is due within 30 days from the end of each quarter, while Integrated Filing (Financial) is due within 45 days from the end of each quarter other than the last quarter, and within 60 days from the end of the last quarter of the financial year. The circular also clarifies that, for the December 2024 quarter, the “governance” and “financial” integrated filings are both covered by that one-time 45-day filing window. The listed entity must submit the integrated filing in PDF on the NSE platform using the new announcement subjects “Integrated Filing- Governance” and “Integrated Filing- Financial,” located under Type of Disclosure: “Others” and Subject Category: “Integrated Filing” at NEAPS > Compliance > Announcements > Announcements/Corporate Action > Create Announcement.

The circular also imposes a specific data-protection requirement: PAN details must be masked in the PDF submissions. In addition, the Exchange states that existing filing obligations remain in place for the underlying items, including corporate governance and investor grievance-related XBRL filings, Regulation 30 event disclosures in PDF/XBRL as applicable, financial results filings, impact of audit qualification (annual), statement of deviations or utilization of funds (SOD), related party transactions (RPT) half-yearly filing, quarterly disclosure of outstanding defaults on loans/debt securities, and board-meeting outcome filings for financials under the current process and timelines. For the December 2024 quarter, the examples given indicate that financial outcome filings and some Regulation 30 event filings continue under their current timelines, while the integrated PDF itself must be filed according to the new schedule. The circular instructs listed entities to comply immediately with these requirements and directs queries to the NSE Listing Compliance team through NEAPS or takeover@nse.co.in.

rows.desc: Non-Confidential Circular Department: Listing Circular Ref No: NSE/CML/2024/32 Date: October 25, 2024 To, The Company Secretary, All Listed Entities Subject: Fetching of document from Tax Service Platform available with Depository by Listed Companies for giving tax claim relief to Foreign Portfolio Investors (FPls) from the perspective of ease of doing business. Dear Sir/ Madam, Pursuant to the amendments made in the Income Tax Act by the Finance Acts, 2020, 2021 and 2023, dividend and interest paid by companies are taxable in the hands of shareholders and bond holders. Further, the companies are required to deduct tax at source (TDS) at the rates applicable to each category of the shareholder. However, certain categories of domestic Investors are exempted while for other categories like Foreign Portfolio Investor (FPIs), tax has to be deducted at 20% (plus surcharge and cess) or at a beneficial tax rate applicable under Double Taxation Avoidance Agreement (DTAA). In case of FPIs, Custodians/FPIs are required to provide certain set of documents like Form 10F, permanent establishment document, tax residency certificate to every company which is declaring dividend/interest to claim tax benefit. With a view to manage the operational challenges of providing same set of client documents/details to every company, NSDL has developed a tax services platform to enable Custodians to upload such client documents once in a financial year which can be accessed by Issuers and Registrars and Transfer Agent (RTAs) for determining the rate for tax deductions. From an ease of doing business perspective, all the Listed Companies are requested to take note of the aforesaid Tax Service Platform for fetching required documents for giving tax claim benefit in respect of tax withheld at source in case of dividend/interest income for FPIs. Yours faithfully, For National Stock Exchange of India Limited Ajit Mahadik Manager – Listing Compliance
rows.summary:

Sr. No Violation by market maker Penalty/disciplinary action 1 First instance reported for the market maker and scrip combination, The Merchant Bankers shall be notified of the non- compliance and advised through an advisory letter to consider appointing new market maker in the non- complied scrip 2 Second instance reported for the same market maker and scrip combination, All ongoing applications (Excluding the open IPOs) involving the concerned Merchant Bankers shall be kept on hold for a period of 1 month and Merchant banker shall be directed to appoint new market maker in the non-complied scrip. 3 Third instance reported for the same market maker and scrip combination, Merchant Bankers shall be debarred from taking on any new assignments for a period of 6 months, including keeping on hold all the ongoing applications (excluding the open IPOs). This shall be reported to SEBI. Disciplinary actions over Market Maker for non-compliances observed in market making activities in SM

rows.summary:
The Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI), acting under Section 101A of the Insurance Act, 1938 and with Central Government approval, has issued the “Obligatory Cession for the financial year 2025–26” notification, applicable to Indian re-insurers and other insurers covered by Section 101A. For business attaching during 1 April 2025 through 31 March 2026, insurers must cede 4% of the sum insured on each general insurance policy to the Indian re-insurer(s); this cession is specifically set at nil for the terrorism premium portion and for premium ceded to the nuclear pool. The entire obligatory cession must be placed only with General Insurance Corporation of India (GIC Re).  

For the 2025–26 cession period, there is no ceiling on the sum insured applicable to cessions, but the Indian re-insurer may require immediate underwriting information notice for any cession above a limit it specifies, and the ceding insurer must provide such information whenever the specified threshold is exceeded. Commission on obligatory cession is prescribed by class of business: at least 5% for Motor TP and Oil & Energy insurance, at least 10% for Group Health insurance, at least 7.50% for Crop Insurance, average terms for Aviation insurance, and at least 15% for all other classes of insurance business; higher commission may be agreed bilaterally between the Indian re-insurer(s) and the ceding insurer.  

The notification also provides for profit commission sharing on a 50:50 basis between the Indian re-insurer and the ceding insurer, based on the performance and surplus of the ceding insurer’s total obligatory portfolio, after taking into account an incurred loss percentage measured at the end of three financial years, management expenses of 2%, profit of 5%, and commission of 12.5%.

rows.summary:
This IRDAI notification, issued on 20 March 2024 and effective from 1 April 2024, formally de-notifies a broad set of previously prevailing tariff products under section 64-ULA(1) of the Insurance Act, 1938. It states that all tariffs notified by the erstwhile Tariff Advisory Committee and still in force are being removed from tariff status, and that coverage for risks falling within those tariff classes will henceforth be governed by the IRDAI (Insurance Products) Regulations, 2024 and the Authority’s Master Circular/Guidelines on products and procedures in general insurance business.

The specific tariff classes de-notified are: the Fire Insurance Tariffs (except the All India Fire Tariff, 2001, which had already been de-tariffed by a 28 December 2020 notification), namely the All India Fire Tariff, Industrial All Risks Tariff, Consequential Loss (Fire) Tariff, Petro-chemical Tariff, and List of Hazardous Goods; the All India Motor Tariff; the Engineering Insurance Tariffs, namely Contractors All Risk Insurance, Contractors Plant and Machinery Insurance, Machinery Breakdown Insurance, Electronic Equipment Insurance, Civil Engineering Completed Risks Insurance, Erection All Risk/Storage Cum Erection Insurance, Loss of profit (MB & BLOP) Insurance, Boiler and Pressure Vessels Insurance, and Deterioration of Stocks-(potato) Insurance; Workmen’s Compensation Insurance Tariffs; and the Tea Tariff under Marine business. From 1 April 2024 onward, these tariffs are “entirely de-notified and no longer in force.”

A key compliance protection is also imposed: no insurer may at any time withdraw, discourage the use of, or decline to offer any customer any of the tariff products that existed before this notification. In other words, although the tariffs themselves cease to have force, insurers must continue to make the underlying products available and cannot refuse to sell or steer customers away from them. The practical consequence for insurers is that pricing, wording, terms, and product handling for affected lines must now be aligned to the IRDAI product regulations and master circular procedures, rather than relying on the old tariff regime, while maintaining customer access to those legacy tariff products.

rows.summary:
The Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI) has issued a notification dated 16 February 2024, effective for the financial year 1 April 2024 through 31 March 2025, under Section 101A of the Insurance Act, 1938. It applies to Indian reinsurers and other insurers covered by Section 101A, and it sets the obligatory cession for each general insurance policy at 4% of the sum insured for policies attaching during FY 2024-25. The only explicit carve-outs are terrorism premium and premium ceded to the nuclear pool, for which the obligatory cession is nil.

The notification states that the entire obligatory cession must be placed with General Insurance Corporation of India (GIC Re) only. It also removes any sum-insured cap for cessions made during the period from 1 April 2024 to 31 March 2025, but allows the Indian reinsurer to require immediate underwriting information for any cession above limits it specifies; the ceding insurer must provide that information whenever those specified thresholds are exceeded.

For commission on the obligatory cession, the notification prescribes minimum rates by class of business: 5% for Motor TP and Oil & Energy insurance, 10% for Group Health insurance, 7.50% for Crop Insurance, average terms for Aviation insurance, and 15% for all other classes of insurance business. Any commission above those minimums may be agreed mutually between the Indian reinsurer(s) and the ceding insurer.

It also provides for profit commission sharing on a 50:50 basis between the Indian reinsurer and the ceding insurer, based on the performance and surplus of the ceding insurer’s total obligatory portfolio. The profit-sharing calculation is to factor in incurred loss percentage, determined at the end of 3 financial years, along with management expenses of 2%, profit of 5%, and commission of 12.5%.

rows.summary:
The Insurance Ombudsman (Amendment) Rules, 2023 were issued by India’s Ministry of Finance on 9 November 2023 under section 24 of the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority Act, 1999, and they take effect immediately on publication in the Official Gazette. The amendments update the 2017 Insurance Ombudsman Rules in several operational areas affecting the Insurance Ombudsman system and the Council for Insurance Ombudsmen. In rule 7(2), references to the “Bank Board Bureau” in clauses (b) and (c) are replaced with “Financial Services Institutions Bureau,” and the rule now expressly defines that term as the body constituted by the Ministry of Finance, Department of Financial Services via Resolution F. No. 14/1/2022-BO-I dated 1 July 2022.

The resignation procedure for an Insurance Ombudsman is changed in rule 8: the Ombudsman may resign by giving at least 90 days’ prior written notice to the Council for Insurance Ombudsmen in lieu of three months’ salary. If the last day of the notice period falls on a Saturday, Sunday, or holiday, the Ombudsman will be relieved on the next working day, and the Council retains discretion to waive the notice period in part or in full. This is a substantive procedural change for appointments and exits of Insurance Ombudsmen and should be reflected in HR/administrative processes.

Rule 10(1) is amended to remove the requirement that any pension payable from the Central Government or a State Government be deducted from the Ombudsman’s salary, changing the compensation treatment for appointees who draw government pensions. Rule 16’s marginal heading is revised to “Complaint settled through mediation by Insurance Ombudsman,” clarifying that the rule now expressly concerns mediation-based settlement. In rule 17, the award issued by the Insurance Ombudsman must now be in writing and must be signed personally or digitally by the Ombudsman, with reasons recorded for the award; and the numeric threshold in the proviso to sub-rule (3), clause (ii), is increased from 30 to 50. The document notes these are amendments to the principal rules originally published on 27 April 2017 and previously amended in 2018, 2021, and May 2021.

For all **general insurance policies attaching during 1 April 2023 through 31 March 2024**, insurers must cede **4% of the sum insured** as obligatory cession to Indian re-insurer(s), but **terrorism premium and premium ceded to the Nuclear pool are excluded and must be treated as NIL cession**. Profit commission is **not payable if the loss ratio exceeds 78%**, and the profit commission itself is capped at **14%**. In practical compliance terms, insurers writing general insurance business for the 2023–24 financial year need to ensure that their obligatory cession processes, documentation, cession placement, information-sharing triggers, and commission accounting are aligned with these mandatory IRDAI requirements.

rows.summary:
This IRDAI amendment, notified on 5 December 2022 and effective from publication in the Official Gazette, updates the **IRDAI (Insurance Intermediaries) Regulations, 2022** by amending two existing 2015 frameworks: the **Registration of Corporate Agents Regulations, 2015** and the **Registration of Insurance Marketing Firm Regulations, 2015**. Its stated policy objective is to give prospects and policyholders broader choice in how they buy insurance through multiple distribution channels and to expand insurance reach and penetration across India. It applies to entities operating as **Corporate Agents** and **Insurance Marketing Firms (IMFs)**, and it changes the scope and applicability rules for both.

For **Corporate Agents**, the amendment replaces Regulation 3 so that a corporate agent can only have arrangements with a capped number of insurers during the validity of its registration certificate. A **Corporate Agent (Life)** may tie up with a maximum of **nine life insurers**; a **Corporate Agent (General)** may tie up with a maximum of **nine general insurers**; and a **Corporate Agent (Health)** may tie up with a maximum of **nine health insurers**, each for soliciting, procuring, and servicing those insurers’ products. The amendment adds a specific activity restriction for general business: a **Corporate Agent (General)** may solicit, procure, and service **retail lines** of general insurance and only those **commercial lines** where the **total sum insured does not exceed ₹5 crores per risk, for all insurances combined**. For a **Corporate Agent (Composite)**, the same per-segment limits apply, but the composite agent may exceed the separate nine-insurer caps only so long as the **total number of arrangements across life, general, and health insurers does not exceed 27 at any point in time**.

For **Insurance Marketing Firms**, the amendment replaces Regulation 3(a)(i) on insurer tie-ups. An IMF may engage Insurance Sales Persons to solicit and procure insurance products from a maximum of **six life insurers, six general insurers, and six health insurers at any point in time**, and it must do so **under intimation to the Authority**. If an insurer relationship changes because of cancellation, termination, or discontinuity, the arrangement must follow the terms of the IMF-insurer agreement, and there must be **suitable arrangements for servicing existing policyholders by the concerned insurer**. The IMF must also **inform IRDAI of any such change in the format specified by the Authority**, so compliance teams should ensure internal controls track insurer tie-ups, manage policyholder servicing continuity, and maintain the prescribed notification process.  

The amendment also changes the **area of operation** rule for IMFs under Regulation 19(3) and Schedule IV: the “Area” is defined as **the State for which the IMF’s registration is valid**. Compliance teams should treat this as a state-specific operating restriction tied to the registration, rather than a broader geographic permission.

rows.summary:
The IRDAI (Other Forms of Capital) Regulations, 2022 establish a new regulatory framework for insurers to issue “Other Forms of Capital” (OFC), and they replace the 2015 OFC regulations. They came into force on the date they were published in the Official Gazette and are stated to remain in force for three years from publication unless reviewed or amended sooner. The stated purpose is to govern issuance of OFC by insurers other than a foreign re-insurer’s branch and to set minimum reporting and disclosure requirements.

Under the regulations, OFC consists only of two instrument types: preference share capital and subordinated debt. Preference shares must satisfy the Companies Act definition and the specific criteria in these regulations, and subordinated debt includes debentures under the Companies Act plus any other debt instrument later permitted by IRDAI. General legal terms not defined in the regulations continue to have the meanings given in the Insurance Act, 1938, the IRDAI Act, 1999, the Companies Act, 2013, and the relevant rules/regulations under those laws.

To qualify as OFC, the instruments must be issued and fully paid up in cash, and their claims must rank behind policyholders and all creditors. Preference shareholders must rank ahead of equity shareholders but behind policyholders and creditors. For subordinated debt, the claims must be subordinated to those of policyholders and all creditors, and also to other specified obligations depending on the instrument structure, consistent with the regulations’ ranking rules. The document also contains additional qualification conditions for OFC instruments, including requirements on voting rights, redemption, conversion, and maturity/profile restrictions, though the excerpt provided is partial.

The regulations impose a minimum regulatory capital framework: insurers may issue OFC only within the limits and conditions set by IRDAI, and the treatment of these instruments for regulatory purposes depends on the instrument type and compliance with the qualifying conditions. A specific quantitative provision appears in the definition of subordinated debt, indicating that any permitted amount/threshold calculations are to be determined within the regulatory framework rather than purely by company choice. The text also references detailed compliance rules for reporting and disclosures, meaning insurers issuing OFC must follow prescribed filing and transparency requirements with IRDAI.

Affected entities are insurers issuing capital instruments in India, excluding foreign re-insurer branches. Compliance teams should note that any existing OFC issuance must be checked against the 2022 rules because the 2015 regulations are superseded. The key operational obligation is to ensure any preference shares or subordinated debt intended to count as OFC are fully cash-paid, correctly ranked in insolvency/claim priority, and otherwise satisfy the regulatory criteria before issuance and on an ongoing basis.

rows.summary:
The IRDAI (Indian Insurance Companies) (Amendment) Regulations, 2021 were issued by the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India on 7 July 2021 and took effect immediately on publication in the Official Gazette. Their stated purpose is to harmonize IRDAI insurance-company regulations with the Insurance (Amendment) Act, 2021 and the Indian Insurance Companies (Foreign Investment) Rules, 2015, by amending several existing regulations that apply to Indian insurance companies.

The most significant change is the insertion of a new regulation 5A in the Registration of Indian Insurance Companies Regulations, 2000 for Indian insurance companies with foreign investment. It requires that a majority of the board directors be Resident Indian Citizens, a majority of Key Management Persons also be Resident Indian Citizens, and at least one of the chairperson, managing director, or chief executive officer must be a Resident Indian Citizen. “Resident Indian Citizen” is defined by reference to rule 2(1)(o) of the Foreign Investment Rules, 2015.

A new regulation 5B is also inserted for Indian insurance companies with foreign investment exceeding 49%. If such a company pays dividend on equity shares in a financial year and, at any time in that year, its solvency margin is below 1.2 times the control level of solvency, then at least 50% of that year’s net profit must be retained in general reserve. In addition, unless the chairperson of the board is an independent director, at least 50% of the directors must be independent directors; if the chairperson is independent, then at least one-third of the board must be independent directors.

The amendment also changes the application/registration filing requirements in regulation 10. The foreign investment threshold in regulation 10(2)(e) is increased from 49% to 74%, clauses (f) and (g) of regulation 10(2) are omitted, and new affidavit requirements are introduced: where the applicant has foreign investment, the managing director, chief executive officer, or whole-time director together with the promoters must file an affidavit certifying compliance with regulation 5A; where the applicant has foreign investment exceeding 49%, a separate affidavit is required confirming compliance with the more stringent requirements applicable to that level of foreign ownership. The document also makes corresponding textual amendments to Regulations 29, 30, and 31, and to other linked provisions, to align those regulations with the new foreign-investment framework and Resident Indian Citizen requirements.

rows.summary:
The Indian Insurance Companies (Foreign Investment) Amendment Rules, 2021, issued by the Ministry of Finance on 19 May 2021, take effect immediately on publication in the Official Gazette. They amend the Indian Insurance Companies (Foreign Investment) Rules, 2015 and were made under section 114(2)(aaa) of the Insurance Act, 1938, read with section 2(7A)(b); the government had earlier published draft rules on 15 April 2021 and considered public comments before finalizing them.

The most significant change is that the foreign investment ceiling in an Indian insurance company is raised from 49% to 74%. The definition provisions are also revised: several definitions in rule 2 are deleted, the definition of “Resident Indian Citizen” is replaced so that it now means what is provided in the Central Government’s current FDI policy, and “Total Foreign Investment” is redefined to mean the sum of direct and indirect foreign investment by foreign investors, calculated in the manner specified by the Authority’s registration regulations. A new interpretive clause is added so that undefined terms take their meanings from the Insurance Act or rules/regulations made under it.

Governance requirements are tightened for insurers with foreign investment. In any Indian insurance company with foreign investment, a majority of directors must be Resident Indian Citizens, a majority of Key Management Persons must be Resident Indian Citizens, and at least one of the chairperson of the board, the managing director, or the chief executive officer must be a Resident Indian Citizen. The rule expressly applies the existing corporate-governance meaning of “Key Management Person.” Companies that already had foreign investment on or before the commencement date must comply with these governance requirements within one year of commencement.

The amendment also adds a new dividend restriction for companies with foreign investment exceeding 49%. For any financial year in which equity-share dividends are paid and at any time during that year the solvency margin is below 1.2 times the control level of solvency, at least 50% of net profit for that financial year must be retained; the text provided cuts off after “not less than fifty per cent. of the net profit for the finan…,” so any remaining sub-clauses are not visible in the excerpt. Compliance teams should therefore treat the visible portion as clearly imposing a profit-retention condition tied to dividend distribution and solvency status, effective from the amendment’s commencement date.

rows.summary:
This IRDAI notification titled **“Obligatory Cession for the financial year 2021-22”** was issued on **28 December 2020** and applies to **Indian re-insurers and other insurers covered under Section 101A of the Insurance Act, 1938**. It sets the compulsory reinsurance cession for policies attaching during the financial year **1 April 2021 through 31 March 2022** at **5% of the sum insured on each General Insurance Policy**, and specifies that this cession is to be placed **only with General Insurance Corporation of India (GIC Re)**. The notification expressly excludes **terrorism premium** and premium ceded to the **Nuclear Pool**, for which the obligatory cession is **nil**.

For the cessions made during this period, the notification states that there is **no limit on sum insured** applicable to obligatory cessions, but the **Indian re-insurer may require immediate underwriting information notice** for any cession exceeding a limit it specifies, and the ceding insurer must provide such information whenever those thresholds are exceeded. This means insurers must be prepared to comply with any information-request threshold set by the Indian re-insurer, even though the regulation itself does not impose a universal monetary cap.

The notification also prescribes **minimum commission rates** on obligatory cession by class of business: **5% minimum for Motor TP and Oil & Energy insurance**, **10% minimum for Group Health insurance**, **7.50% minimum for Crop Insurance**, **average terms for Aviation insurance**, and **15% minimum for all other classes of insurance business**. It further allows any commission above these minimums only by **mutual agreement between the Indian re-insurer(s) and the ceding insurer**.  

On **profit commission**, the Indian re-insurer must share profit commission with the ceding insurer on a **50:50 basis**, based on the performance and surplus of the ceding insurer’s total obligatory portfolio, after taking into account: **incurred loss percentage measured at the end of 3 financial years**, **management expenses at 2%**, **profit at 5%**, **commission at 15%**, and a **loss ratio range of 50% to 78%**. No profit commission is payable if the **loss ratio exceeds 78%**, and the **profit commission is capped at 14%**.

The Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI) has upgraded its Business Analytics Platform (BAP) and is moving several reinsurance-related regulatory processes onto that integrated portal to support streamlined regulatory reporting and related reinsurance functions. The migration covers Reinsurance Regulatory Returns, Reinsurance Summary Formats for both Advance and Final submissions, and applications for issuance of File Reference Numbers (FRNs) for Cross Border Reinsurers (CBRs); it also newly brings into BAP applications relating to appointment and remuneration of the Chairperson/CEO of reinsurers and foreign reinsurer branches (FRBs). As a result, all insurers, reinsurers, foreign reinsurer branches (including Lloyd’s India and its constituents), and other affected entities must now use the integrated Reinsurance BAP portal for these submissions rather than separate legacy processes.

The circular specifies the following filing applicability dates: Reinsurance Regulatory Returns must be submitted on BAP starting from FY 2024–25; Pool Administrator Returns also from FY 2024–25; Corporate Governance Returns from FY 2025–26; and Reinsurance Programme Summary Returns and Final Reinsurance Programme Summary Returns from FY 2026–27. Requests for approvals concerning appointment and remuneration of CEOs/KMPs and FRN requests for CBRs are also to be handled through BAP, without a separate fiscal-year start date stated in the text. IRDAI states that operational guidelines and instructions for all reinsurance-related functions will be made available on the BAP portal for users, so compliance teams should review the portal instructions before filing. The circular is issued with the approval of the Competent Authority and is dated 28 August 2026.

rows.summary:
IRDAI has issued a circular dated **27 August 2026** permitting **all insurers** to invest in **“Maharajah INR Bonds” / “Onshore Rupee Bonds” issued by the New Development Bank (NDB)** as part of their **approved investments**. NDB has proposed to raise **INR 25,000 crores over a five-year period**, and the stated use of proceeds is for **general corporate purposes** and for **financing/onward lending to sustainable development, sustainable infrastructure, and green/social projects in India**.

The circular states that these NDB rupee bond issuances are treated as **“securities” under the Securities Contracts (Regulation) Act, 1956**, and may be invested in by insurers only if several conditions are met. Specifically, the bonds must be governed by any applicable **Government of India norms**, the **public issue must be approved by SEBI**, insurers must comply with **Section 27E of the Insurance Act, 1938**, and the bonds must satisfy the **rating criteria for “Approved Investments” under Schedule III of the IRDAI (Actuarial, Finance and Investment Functions of Insurers) Regulations, 2024**, as amended from time to time. If SEBI exempts the rating requirement because the bond has been rated by an **international rating agency**, then that **equivalent rating** will be accepted for this purpose.

The circular also creates an **infrastructure-investment qualification**: if the bond proceeds are deployed into **infrastructure sub-sectors notified under the Ministry of Finance’s Harmonized Master List**, then investments in those bonds will count as **“infrastructure investments.”** IRDAI has assigned the following category codes for compliance and reporting purposes: **EORB** for **Onshore Rupee Bonds issued by NDB** as approved investments, **IORB** for **Onshore Rupee Bonds issued by NDB (Infrastructure-approved)**, **OORB** for **Onshore Rupee Bonds issued by NDB** under other investments, and **IOOB** for **Onshore Rupee Bonds issued by NDB (Infrastructure-others)**. The circular is issued under **clause 12(6) of Schedule III of the IRDAI (Actuarial, Finance and Investment Functions of Insurers) Regulations, 2024**.

IRDAI has issued a circular dated 07-08-2026 (Ref. IRDAI/F&I/CIR/MISC/102/8/2026) requiring insurers to begin monthly submission of specified data for the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation’s Index of Service Production (ISP). IRDAI specifically advises insurers to ensure the information is **complete and accurate at the time of submission**. This circular is issued under **Section 14(2)(h) of the IRDA Act, 1999** solely to support ISP data collection, and IRDAI expressly states that it **does not alter any existing disclosure requirements or financial statement preparation requirements** under the **Insurance Act, 1938**, the **IRDA Act, 1999**, or regulations made under those laws.

rows.summary:
IRDAI has issued Circular No. IRDAI/NL/GDL/98(01)/07/2026 dated 31 July 2026 to all CEOs/CMDs of insurance companies, including life and standalone health insurers, directing them to take immediate special measures for claims arising from the floods and declared natural disaster affecting the Assam districts of Sivasagar, Charaideo, Jorhat, and Golaghat, with the floods stated to have commenced on 19 July 2026. The circular requires insurers to mobilize all available resources immediately, including surveyors and investigators, and to appoint senior Nodal Officers to oversee claims handling in the affected areas; the appointment of the Nodal Officer must be communicated immediately to the Chief Secretary, and claims in each district may also be handled by a designated District Claims Service Head.

Insurers must activate and publicize 24x7 customer support/helplines to assist claimants, and they are expected to launch a broad awareness campaign about the assistance being provided. The circular specifically directs insurers to publish the contact details of district heads on their websites and to give appropriate publicity through press and digital media.

For claims handling, insurers are instructed to use special empowered district desks to ensure prompt surveys and speedy processing, including on-account/interim payments where needed to support early reinstatement of property or business. The circular emphasizes that all claims should be surveyed immediately and both claim payments and interim payments should be disbursed at the earliest possible time. Insurers should encourage policyholders to communicate electronically wherever possible when initiating claims and submitting documents, and they should use digital processes to the extent possible for claim assessment.

The circular also directs insurers to streamline documentation so that only information necessary to substantiate the claim amount is collected, with the goal of expediting final settlement. In death claims where a death certificate is difficult to obtain because the body has not been recovered, the claim may still be processed without insisting on a death certificate if the insured’s details match the details of the deceased published by the State/Central Government or another appropriate government authority.

Finally, IRDAI requires all insurers—life, general, and health—to submit weekly claims data in the prescribed format enclosed with the circular. The document does not specify a final sunset date, but the operational obligations are immediate and ongoing for claims arising from this disaster.

rows.summary:
IRDAI has issued a circular to **all insurers except reinsurers** requiring them to speed up and standardize their responses to requests from the **Office of the Insurance Ombudsman (IO)**. The regulator says it has observed repeated delays in insurers submitting **Self-Contained Notes (SCNs)**, supporting documents, and follow-up information, often in piecemeal form, which is delaying disposal of policyholder/beneficiary complaints.

The circular ties these obligations to the **Insurance Ombudsman Rules, 2017**, especially **Rule 15(2)** (documents/information the Ombudsman may seek) and **Rule 17(4)**, which requires a complaint to be decided within **90 days of receipt of all required material from the complainant**. To support that timeline, insurers are now advised to submit the required **SCN with relevant documents within 7 days** of receiving notice from the relevant Ombudsman office, and to provide any additional information or documents requested under Rule 15(2) **within 3 days** of the notice.

IRDAI also explicitly requires insurers to submit all requested material **in one go rather than in multiple piecemeal submissions**. In addition, insurers must **clear all pending SCN requests and outstanding requests for additional information/documents within 30 days of the circular’s issue date (July 23, 2026)**. If an insurer does not comply, the Ombudsman office may proceed **ex parte**—that is, decide the matter without further waiting, based only on the material available on record—to preserve the Rule 17(4) timeline.

rows.summary:
This IRDAI circular, dated 14 July 2026 and addressed to all insurers, issues additional clarifications on implementation of Indian Accounting Standards (Ind AS), building on Circular No. IRDAI/F&I/CIR/MISC/45/4/2026 dated 1 April 2026. The clarifications are intended to ensure consistent implementation of the regulatory framework and specifically address three areas: the role of the Appointed Actuary, the requirement for independent validation, and the preparation of Ind AS-compliant financial statements for consolidation purposes.

On the Appointed Actuary’s role, the circular states that under Clauses 6 and 7 of Part II of Schedule I of the IRDAI (Actuarial, Finance and Investment Functions of Insurers) Regulations, 2024, the Appointed Actuary must provide actuarial expertise, advice, and other actuarial inputs needed to prepare financial statements under the applicable Ind AS. This includes actuarial valuation and measurement of policy liabilities under Ind AS 117, liabilities arising from investment contracts under Ind AS 109, and service contracts under Ind AS 115; determining and reviewing the actuarial methodologies and assumptions used; providing actuarial input for disclosures relating to insurance contracts and reinsurance contracts held; and any other actuarial matters needed for compliance with Ind AS, IRDAI regulations/circulars/directions, and IAI professional standards/guidance notes. The Appointed Actuary must also submit a technical report to the Board covering the actuarial valuation of policy liabilities used in preparing Ind AS financial statements; the report must set out the material methodologies, assumptions, judgements, reliance on management or other internal information, and compliance with applicable IAI standards/guidance, plus any other matters the actuary considers material. For first-time adoption of Ind AS, the report must also reconcile policy liabilities under the previous accounting framework (Schedule II of the 2024 regulations) to the Ind AS policy liabilities and explain the material differences. The report must be placed before the Board, and the Board-approved copy must be submitted to IRDAI along with the annual financial statements.

For independent validation, the circular requires every insurer to obtain an independent validation of the process used to implement the applicable Ind AS during the first year of implementation. This requirement applies in FY 2026–27 for insurers implementing Ind AS from FY 2026–27, and in FY 2027–28 for insurers that have been granted forbearance. The document also clarifies earlier paragraph 8 of the 1 April 2026 circular, indicating that the timing and applicability of the validation obligation depend on the insurer’s implementation timeline and whether forbearance has been granted.

The circular also modifies the earlier transitional/finalization expectations for financial statements in connection with consolidation. It refers to insurers preparing Ind AS-compliant financial statements for consolidation purposes and provides clarification under the regulatory framework, including references to the 2024 Actuarial, Finance and Investment Functions Regulations and to subsequent implementation guidance. Because the excerpt provided cuts off mid-paragraph after reference to the earlier circular, the full detail of this consolidation-related clarification is not visible in the text supplied; however, the circular clearly signals that insurers must align their Ind AS implementation, actuarial reporting, Board review, and independent validation with the stated FY 2026–27 / FY 2027–28 timelines and the specified reporting submission requirements.

rows.summary:
IRDAI has issued a circular dated **8 July 2026** to **all insurers and reinsurers** updating the **formats for publishing financial results to stock exchanges under SEBI’s LODR Regulations, 2015**. The change is driven by the adoption of **Ind AS by insurers**: for insurers that are required to prepare financial statements under Ind AS, the existing stock-exchange reporting formats have been revised for **unaudited/audited quarterly financial results**. In particular, such listed **life insurers, general insurers, health insurers, and reinsurers** must now use **Annexure I** for quarterly financial results, **Annexure II** for segment-wise revenue, results, and capital employed with the quarterly results, **Annexure III** for limited review reports, **Annexure IV** for audit reports in audited financial reports, and **Annexure V** for the newspaper publication required under **Regulation 47(1)(b)** of LODR.

The circular makes an important carve-out for insurers that have been **granted forbearance for FY 2026–27 for Ind AS implementation**. Those insurers, if they are instead required to prepare financial statements under **Schedule II of the IRDAI (Actuarial, Finance and Investment Functions of Insurers) Regulations, 2024**, must **continue using the existing formats under the earlier IRDAI circulars** rather than the new annexures. The two continuing references are **Circular No. IRDA/F&I/REG/CIR/208/10/2016 dated 25 October 2016** and **Circular No. IRDA/F&A/CIR/LFTD/027/01/2017 dated 30 January 2017**.

For compliance purposes, this circular is explicitly stated to be issued **only to help listed insurers and reinsurers satisfy SEBI disclosure requirements under LODR**. It does **not** change the underlying requirements for preparing financial statements under the **Insurance Act, 1938**, the **IRDA Act, 1999**, or the regulations made under those laws. In practice, a compliance team should therefore determine first whether the entity is an **Ind AS-reporting listed insurer/reinsurer** or an entity covered by the **FY 2026–27 forbearance**, and then ensure the correct reporting format is used for stock-exchange filings and newspaper publication accordingly.
